This example simplifies the nursing market by focusing onthe"average”nurse.In reality,of course,the marketfor nurses is actuallymadeupofmany smallermarkets, likemarketsfor nurses with varying degreesof experienceandcredentials.Manymarketscontaincloselyrelated productsthatdifferinquality;forinstance,even a simple product like gasoline comes in regular, premium, and super-premium, each with a different price. Even in such cases, discussing the average price of gasoline, like the average salary for nurses, can stil be useful because it reflects what is happening in most of the submarkets.
